Lucretius

Quotes / Lucretius / Q0229

English

Pleasant it is, when winds trouble the great sea, to gaze from shore upon another's great tribulation.
Thinker Lucretius
School Epicureanism
Source De Rerum Natura II.1–2
Theme Philosophy
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

This English passage is associated with De Rerum Natura II.1–2, within the tradition of Epicureanism. The wording below is a verified rendering prepared for careful reading rather than a claim of unique translation authority.

A short reading

Read in the register of philosophy, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Lucretius's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
